newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alumbrera starts copper concentrator.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alumbrera starts copper concentrator.

text.p: Argentina's first modern copper mine, the giant Bajo de la Alumbrera, has begun operating its concentrator, industry sources said Tuesday.
No mine official could immediately be contacted to confirm the report.
The $1.05-1.1 billion mine in the northwestern desert province of Catamarca is designed to produce an annual average of 180,000 tonnes of copper and 640,000 ounces of gold over 20 years.
Australia's MIM Holdings has 50 percent of the project. North Ltd, also of Australia, and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd, each have 25 percent.
